sourceOfTruth:
Three state owners, one per code finding — each is the mutator, not a nearby convenience predicate.

(1) DEPLOY GRAPH — owner: `apps/website/vercel.json` key `buildCommand`, the single string that decides WHICH producer resolves the workspace build graph on Vercel. The resolver that owns the `@pair/website -> @pair/content-ops` edge is turbo (`turbo.json` `build.dependsOn: ["^build"]`), so the oracle is turbo's own resolved task graph (`--dry=json`), NOT `apps/website/package.json`'s `build` script (which is a leaf that resolves nothing) and NOT the CI `build` job (which already goes through turbo and is green either way).

(2) LINK SURFACE — owner: `maskLiteralConstructs` + `CODE_SPAN_RE` in `apps/website/lib/docs-staleness-check.ts:289-311,420`, the function that MUTATES the scanned surface (blanks bytes). `linkSurface`'s block grouping, `findDeadRepoLinks` (Check 5b) and `findDeadLinks` (Check 5) are consumers of that mutation, not owners. Authoritative grammar: CommonMark § 6.1 code spans — a closer is a backtick run of EXACTLY the opener's length. Authoritative renderer/consumer (per ADL 2026-09-04 "the link surface's oracle is the site build"): the repo's own installed MDX pipeline `@mdx-js/mdx@3.1.1` compiled with `remark-gfm@4.0.1`, counting `href:` in the emitted JSX; cross-checked against `gh api -X POST /markdown`.

(3) CORPUS SELECTION — owner: `ORACLE_SELECTION_SIGNALS` in `apps/website/lib/anchor-oracle-selection.ts:27-43` (`isBlockStructureSensitive` is a `.some()` over it, and `scripts/generate-anchor-oracle.ts` gates every `git ls-files '*.md' '*.mdx'` entry on it). The STATE whose sensitivity it classifies is fence parity, owned by the FENCE branch (`closesFence`) of `readMarkdown` in `packages/content-ops/src/markdown/commonmark-blocks.ts` — so the selection rows are derived from CommonMark § 4.5 (fence opener = 3+ backticks or 3+ tildes, indent <= 3), not from the four shipped signals. The anchor ANSWER's oracle is github.com's `/markdown` renderer read as `(id|name)="user-content-…"` in document order — the same oracle the generator uses.
